## Simple explanation

Deep learning is a type of machine learning that uses neural networks with
multiple layers to learn representations from data. It is used in areas
such as language, vision, speech, and multimodal systems.

## Technical explanation

Deep-learning models are parameterized compositions of operations,
typically trained by optimizing a loss with gradient-based methods and
backpropagation. Their performance depends on architecture, data,
objectives, compute, and evaluation—not depth alone.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Many current AI capabilities rely on deep-learning models. Engineers need
to understand how data, compute, training, inference, and evaluation
interact to build systems that are useful and maintainable.

## How it works

The model processes inputs through layers of learned transformations. A
training objective measures error, and an optimizer updates parameters
using gradients computed by backpropagation. At inference, the trained
parameters are used to produce predictions or generated outputs.

## Practical example

A deep-learning image classifier can use a convolutional neural network
or a vision Transformer to predict image classes. Transfer learning can
adapt a pretrained model to a smaller labeled dataset.

## Common misconceptions

- Deep learning is a subset of machine learning, not a synonym for all AI.
- More layers or parameters do not automatically improve results.
- A model that performs well on training data may still fail on new or
  shifted data.
